notes: Protocol incident: two duplicate launches were killed by a platform concurrency cap mid-run and left partial artifacts; the affected participant (leonui/todo) was re-run from a clean slate and an orphan tabs.html was discarded. All reported runs are the clean runs; raw logs are committed beside the pages.

All 8 participants reported their verifier green on cycle 1 — nobody iterated. The grader then failed 2 of the 8 pages. Every failure is an escaped defect: verifier-green, checker-clean, warns-empty, and functionally broken.

Both leonui escapes are runtime-semantics traps, not grammar misuse — neither ui check nor window.__ui.warns can name them today. (a) todo: `set item.done = !item.done` inside a ui:each row copy-on-writes the row's item signal; the array still holds done=false, so the next array replacement — removing a different row — reverts the toggled row. Confirmed by dumping the array signal directly. (b) form: binds track dependencies once at attach; notify-triggered re-runs execute untracked, so they never re-subscribe. With && short-circuiting, `submitted && !nameBad && !emailBad && !ageBad ? 'Welcome…' : ''` boot-subscribes only to `submitted`; after an invalid submit flips it true, later error-flag changes notify signals with zero subscribers and the welcome line can never render. Single-submit flows work; the invalid-then-valid flow does not.

React's reactivity is structurally immune to both trap shapes (a state change re-renders whatever reads it), which is why the same task set escapes nothing there — at the cost of a runtime that is several times larger (see the size table above).

Adaptations worth reading: the leonui/filter agent solved case-insensitivity inside the whitelist by storing three case variants per product (name/l/u) since no lower() operator exists; both react agents, told their console-only verifier cannot exercise interactions, chose uncontrolled inputs read at submit/click time to be robust against React's change-event dedup.
This is a pilot: 4 tasks, one model, one harness. It names two concrete framework defects and gives a baseline; it does not rank the frameworks.
